items.stem: A denial-of-service attack makes a website unavailable to users. Which part of the CIA triad does it primarily attack?

options.rationale: Correct: a denial-of-service attack targets availability by blocking legitimate access.
Confidentiality concerns unauthorised disclosure, not availability.
Integrity concerns unauthorised modification, not access being blocked.
Authentication is a control, not one of the three CIA properties.

items.explanation: Correct: a denial-of-service attack targets availability by blocking legitimate access.

items.stem: Which of the following are strong defences against account takeover? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: MFA blocks most attacks that rely on a stolen password alone.

options.text: Using unique passwords stored in a password manager
options.rationale: Correct: unique passwords stop one breach from unlocking many accounts.

options.text: Reusing one strong password everywhere for convenience
options.rationale: Reuse means one breach compromises every account.

options.text: Emailing the password to yourself as a backup
options.rationale: Email is not a secure store and can itself be compromised.

items.explanation: Correct: MFA blocks most attacks that rely on a stolen password alone.

items.stem: Why do offline or immutable backups specifically help against ransomware?

options.text: They cannot be encrypted or deleted by malware that reaches the live network
options.rationale: Correct: backups the attacker cannot reach allow recovery without paying.
Backup type does not affect network speed and is unrelated to the threat.

options.text: They stop phishing emails from arriving
options.rationale: Backups aid recovery; they do not block the initial phishing vector.
Backups store data copies; they do not manage passwords.

items.explanation: Correct: backups the attacker cannot reach allow recovery without paying.
